problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Eigenvectors of a 3x3 Matrix With Distinct Eigenvalues

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is an upper triangular matrix, we have that its eigenvalues are the entries in the main diagonal, that is, ${\lambda }_{1}=2,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=3.$ 

Also, since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=3.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & -3 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -4{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the augmented matrix $M$ is already in its row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=\frac{5}{4}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} \\  & =4(\frac{5}{4}{x}_{3})-3{x}_{3} \\  & =5{x}_{3}-3{x}_{3} \\  & =2{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ \frac{5}{4}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=4,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{8}{4}=2.$
